correctness.rationale: Verified the link of every vertex under phi_0 is 2-regular, hence a union of cycles. For degree <=k-1 the closed neighborhood has <=k nonremovable vertices; at degree k, an induced link cycle or a K4 yields a nonremovable <=k set, proving delta>=k+1 for k>=4. Combine with orientable Euler edge inequality E<=3v-6+6g to derive g>=1+(k-5)v/12. Independent exact graph reconstruction: the 12-vertex icosahedron has degree 5, exactly two triangles per edge, no nonremovable subset of <=4 vertices, and 12 nonremovable 5-vertex subsets; T_6 (36 vertices) has degree 6, exactly two triangles per edge, no nonremovable subset of <=5 vertices. The all-m torus witness follows the lattice lift and absence of induced 4/5 cycles, not just finite test. The planar 12-vertex uniqueness uses degree saturation and two-triangle links; small cases and exact boundary accounted for.
